neighbours.label: 'with' (or '(') introducing a collaborating partner (together with, in cooperation with, coauthor (with ...))
fire: The vaccine trial was run jointly with three regional hospitals.
The museum organized the exhibit in collaboration with local artists.
She is the coauthor (with her former advisor) of a popular textbook.
The city is building the new bridge in partnership with a private firm.
Our lab worked together with the ministry to collect the samples.
The festival is held in association with the national film board.
The treaty was drafted in cooperation with neighboring countries.
He co-founded the company with two college friends in 2004.
quiet: The vaccine trial was run with a very small budget.
The museum organized the exhibit with great care and attention.
She is the author of a popular textbook on organic chemistry.
The city is building the new bridge with steel from a local mill.
Our lab measured the samples with a new electron microscope.
The festival is held with free entry on the final day.
The treaty was printed with gold letters on heavy paper.
He filled the company's office with plants and old books.

notes: Card: ' with' x8, ' (' x4, cooperation, partnership, 'en conjunto con'. Negative pole is also mostly ' with' but relational/other uses, so the near misses keep 'with' in non-partner senses.
